record.context_brief: Monotone total positivity for Eulerian minors
record.original_question: For all i,j,r in N, consider the square submatrix of the Eulerian matrix A = (A(n+1,k))_{n,k in N} cut out by rows i, i+1, ..., i+r and columns j, j+1, ..., j+r. Is its determinant always a monotonically increasing function of i?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.13. For all i,j,r in N the determinant of the submatrix determined by the rows indexed by i, i+1, ..., i+r and columns indexed by j, j+1, ..., j+r is a monotonically increasing function of i in N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let the Eulerian numbers $A(n,k)$ for integers $n\ge 1$ and $0\le k\le n-1$ be defined by the recurrence
$$A(n,k) = (k+1)\,A(n-1,k) + (n-k)\,A(n-1,k-1),$$
with $A(1,0)=1$ and $A(n,k)=0$ for $k<0$ or $k\ge n$. Equivalently, $A(n,k)$ counts the permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ with exactly $k$ descents.

Form the infinite matrix $\mathcal{A} = (a_{n,k})_{n,k\in\mathbb{N}}$ indexed by $n,k\in\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ by setting
$$a_{n,k} = A(n+1,\,k),$$
so that row $n$ consists of the Eulerian numbers of order $n+1$.

For nonnegative integers $i,j,r$, let
$$M_{i,j,r} := \det\bigl(a_{i+s,\,j+t}\bigr)_{0\le s,t\le r}$$
denote the determinant of the $(r+1)\times(r+1)$ contiguous submatrix of $\mathcal{A}$ with rows $i,i+1,\dots,i+r$ and columns $j,j+1,\dots,j+r$.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed $j,r\in\mathbb{N}$, the function $i\mapsto M_{i,j,r}$ is monotonically increasing in $i\in\mathbb{N}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as a conjecture in a recent (2024) collection of open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality. No subsequent paper resolving this specific monotone-minor conjecture for the Eulerian matrix was found. While total positivity of related Eulerian/amazing matrices has been studied, the monotonicity in the row index of all contiguous minors appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality
status_evidence.snippet: Presenting open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality along with main partial results and computational evidence.
status_evidence.claim: The monotone-minor statement is stated as an open conjecture in this 2024 problem list.

status_evidence.title: Proof of a conjecture on the total positivity of amazing matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Total positivity results for amazing matrices related to Eulerian numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Related total positivity results exist, but do not address monotonicity in i of contiguous Eulerian minors.
